anomaly_def.Name: Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Composite Definition: The database is concurrently affected by mis-tuned engine runtime parameters and impending or actual exhaustion of physical or logical storage space, causing both resource-governance inefficiencies and hard space limits to surface at the same time.

Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly: Critical settings for memory, checkpoints, background workers, parallelism, logging, or connection limits are misaligned with hardware capacity, workload patterns, or version defaults, degrading performance even when raw resources are available.
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly: The data, log, temporary, or backup areas approach or reach full utilization, producing allocation failures, auto-extend errors, and write stalls unrelated to bandwidth limitations.

Combined Phenomena: When these two root causes overlap, the system exhibits a mixture of misleading and self-reinforcing symptoms—e.g., frequent checkpoint storms caused by undersized log files co-occurring with actual log-destination fullness; intense log write waits, buffer flush surges, or autovacuum/autopurge backlogs while I/O devices appear under-utilised; sudden query or DDL failures due to "out of space" errors intermixed with erratic latency from over-aggressive background processes; and oscillating CPU usage as incorrectly configured work-memory or parallelism triggers repeated spill-to-disk operations that then fail or stall because temporary space is depleted. Monitoring dashboards may show paradoxical metrics such as low CPU or I/O throughput alongside severe wait events and aborted transactions.

Causal Chain Analysis: Misconfigured parameters can accelerate space consumption (e.g., excessive log generation from too-frequent checkpoints, bloated temp segments from oversized work memory, or unbounded session counts each creating temp files). At the same time, shrinking free space constrains the database’s ability to honor configuration settings that rely on disk growth (log file extensions, temp-space allocation, auto-grow datafiles), forcing the engine into emergency or aggressive housekeeping modes that further increase I/O and CPU pressure. The feedback loop between poor configuration and dwindling storage manifests as amplified contention, unexpected throttling, and ultimately service outages, making root-cause isolation difficult without recognizing that both parameter mis-tuning and space depletion are jointly responsible.

entry.official_definition: Aborts any statement that takes more than the specified amount of time; zero disables the timeout.
entry.trigger_condition: A SQL statement runs longer than statement_timeout, measured from command arrival until completion.
entry.workload_impact: The running statement is aborted; when configured, the timed-out statement is logged.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when statement execution exceeds a configured execution-time budget because the operation runs too long or the workload is blocked behind other work.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect query shape, access path quality, resource contention, and whether the timeout threshold should be reviewed together with the workload pattern.
